episodes.title: The Epstein Files Are Back: Joyce Vance & Kim Atkins Stohr | #SistersInLaw Podcast
episodes.description:
Ever wondered what happens when a smart lawyer wields a legal scalpel instead of a sledgehammer? Today, we're diving into a blockbuster ruling that’s shaking up transparency laws and could set a precedent for future government accountability.

In this episode:
Katie Phang’s bold lawsuit against the DOJ over Epstein files and why it’s a legal game-changer
How Judge Sullivan’s order requires the DOJ to hand over specific, redacted documents by July 2nd
The strategic choices behind asking for narrowly focused documents instead of broad sweeping disclosures
The significance of standing in legal battles and how Katie proved her injury under the Administrative Procedure Act
The government's weak response, lack of legal justifications, and what this means for transparency laws
Possible next steps: Will the government appeal, and can they get a stay pending the appeal?
Why this case isn’t just about Epstein — it’s about whether Congress can enforce transparency on government actions
